title: How households and school communities adapt behaviour after waste-disposal charging and stronger recycling expectations
topic_description: Waste charging and recycling rules now affect daily routines in Hong Kong estates and school catchments. Your focus group includes student councillors, a parent governor, and a teacher representative. Debate how far schools should monitor families’ sorting behaviour, what support cramped households need, and how to avoid stigma while improving compliance.
instructions: You have 1 minute to prepare and 8 minutes for the group discussion (10 minutes for a group of 4). You should interact with your fellow candidates. Do not read out prepared notes. You may make notes during the preparation time, but you should not write out everything you plan to say.
discussion_points: Whether schools should require household waste logs or rely on voluntary schemes linked to education campaigns.
Fair allocation of subsidies, bags, and multilingual guidance for subdivided flats and shift-working families.
Balancing accountability (contamination fines) with empathy when students come from different housing conditions.
individual_response_questions: How can Hong Kong balance municipal waste targets with privacy concerns about data on household disposal habits?
To what extent should penalties for contamination be delayed until public education has reached vulnerable communities?
hkeaa_alignment: Paper 4: sustained interaction, ideas development, strategies for agreeing, interrupting politely, repairing misunderstanding; intelligibility and communicative effectiveness.
success_feedback: You handled a socially sensitive policy topic with interactional awareness.
suggested_next_steps: Watch a news segment on waste charging; note three useful collocations.
